quiz.title: Unit 8 SAQ 02
quiz.headline: The Cold War and the new states
quiz.prompt: Answer all parts of the question.
quiz.instructions: Answer all three parts. For each part, Answer the question directly, Prove it with specific historical evidence, and Explain how the evidence supports your answer. On the AP exam each part earns one point. This is self-assessment practice, not official College Board scoring.
quiz.note: Original Page One practice in AP short-answer format. Model answers show one strong response; other accurate, well-supported answers can earn the point.

scaffold.label: Answer
scaffold.text: Respond directly to the task verb: identify, describe, or explain.

scaffold.label: Prove
scaffold.text: Name a specific person, place, institution, or development.

scaffold.label: Explain
scaffold.text: Show how or why the evidence answers the question.

parts.prompt: Identify ONE way the United States and the Soviet Union competed without fighting each other directly during the Cold War.
criteria: Names a specific form of competition.
Connects it to the rivalry between the two superpowers.

model.answer: The superpowers competed in an arms race.
model.prove: Both built thousands of nuclear weapons, and each developed long-range missiles after the Soviet Union tested an atomic bomb in 1949 and launched Sputnik in 1957.
model.explain: Each side feared falling behind, so spending on weapons increased and the threat of mutual destruction shaped decisions in crises.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also identify the space race, economic aid to other countries, propaganda, or support for rival governments in other countries.

parts.prompt: Describe ONE conflict in which the superpowers supported opposing sides during the Cold War.
criteria: Describes which sides each superpower supported.

model.answer: In the Korean War, the superpowers supported opposing governments.
model.prove: The Soviet Union and China backed communist North Korea, while the United States led a United Nations force that defended South Korea from 1950 to 1953.
model.explain: The war ended in a stalemate and left Korea divided, showing how Cold War rivalry could turn a local conflict into a larger war.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also describe the Vietnam War, in which the Soviet Union and China aided North Vietnam while the United States supported South Vietnam, or the Soviet–Afghan War of the 1980s.

parts.prompt: Explain ONE way the Cold War affected newly independent states between 1945 and 1975.
criteria: Names a specific state, movement, or policy.
Explains how the Cold War shaped its options.

model.answer: Some new states joined the Non-Aligned Movement to avoid choosing a side.
model.prove: Leaders such as Jawaharlal Nehru of India, Gamal Abdel Nasser of Egypt, and Sukarno of Indonesia met at the Bandung Conference in 1955 and helped found the Non-Aligned Movement in 1961.
model.explain: Nonalignment let new states seek aid from both blocs and gave them more independence in foreign policy than alliance with either superpower would have.

parts.alternatives: Answers can also explain how the superpowers gave economic or military aid to rival governments, as in the Congo or Angola, or supported coups against leaders they distrusted.
